Screenshots and screen recording apps

The AI reads your screenshot as a pixel blob and guesses which button you meant. SlimSnap converts the screenshot plus your annotation into structured JSON: every element has coordinates, an ID, and your arrow points at a specific one. Around 700 tokens vs 1,568 raw on Sonnet. Free Mac app. Schema and Claude Code skill are open MIT. Runs entirely on-device.

Eney [...] The day I shipped this started with me yelling at Claude Code for the fifth time. I'd pasted a screenshot of a misaligned form. I'd typed "fix this." Claude moved the wrong input. I retyped. Claude moved a different wrong input. I gave up and fixed it manually. The reason it kept guessing: it was reading raw pixels. It had no way to know which rectangle was the input I meant, so it picked one that looked plausible. SlimSnap converts the screenshot into a spec the AI can parse element by element. Each element has coordinates, OCR text, color values, and (if you drew an arrow on it) a target reference saying "this one." Ismail Haddou [...] Hi Product Hunt! I’m Ismail, founder and CEO of Pickle.  
  
I use agents for a lot of my own work, but whenever they use a browser they end up wasting tokens reading HTML, so I built a browser that simplifies webpage content for them. It's free, and compatible with Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Codex CLI.  
  
A few key things about it:   
 Full visibility, always. Every action is policy gated, purchases and destructive steps need your approval, everything is logged, and you can watch it happen live on screen.  
 Works with any agent. Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, and Codex CLI today, and anything else that speaks MCP. Nothing to reconfigure. [...] Works with weak models too. Pickle bundles Ollama, so a small local model can run the agent without an API key or the cloud. Weak models get constrained prompting that limits them to one choice at a time, so they don't hallucinate actions or element IDs. Stronger models get full multi-step planning.  
 Reads pages efficiently. Pickle cuts token usage by 32x.  
 Full browser, not just a wrapper. Tabs, history, bookmarks, real Chromium, plus persistent element memory across sessions and a shared notebook the agent and you both write to.  
 Who is Pickle for?  
Anyone running an agent that needs to act in a browser and wants to see what it’s doing before it acts. If you connect Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code, or Codex CLI to real tasks, this is for you.
